title: A realization weak equivalence between Kan complexes has a simplicial homotopy inverse
statement: Use small simplicial sets, Kan complexes, standard simplices and geometric realization of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $f:A\to B$ be a map of Kan complexes whose realization induces a bijection on path components and isomorphisms on all based homotopy groups at every basepoint of $|A|$. Then there exist a simplicial map $g:B\to A$ and simplicial maps $H:A\times\Delta^1\to A$ and $J:B\times\Delta^1\to B$ such that $H|_{A\times\{0\}}=gf$, $H|_{A\times\{1\}}=\mathrm{id}_A$, $J|_{B\times\{0\}}=fg$ and $J|_{B\times\{1\}}=\mathrm{id}_B$. Neither connectedness nor nonemptiness is required.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.7.13, converse (Kan complexes), Kerodon Tag 00UB; Corollary 3.6.4.3, Kerodon Tag 03X7, for the realization convention. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag for this simplicial Whitehead theorem; these are Kerodon tags.

proof.text:
In the degreewise product/pullback convention of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], put
$$P=A\times_{B,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,B).$$
Identify an $n$-simplex of $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,B)$ with a map $\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\to B$ by the natural factor interchange from the definition $\Delta^1\times\Delta^n\to B$; this interchange commutes with all simplicial operators. Write $r:P\to A$ for projection, $p:P\to B$ for endpoint $1$, and $i:A\to P$ for $a\mapsto(a,\mathrm{const}_{f(a)})$. These are simplicial maps: evaluation, projection and constant paths commute with every simplicial operator. Directly $ri=1_A$ and $pi=f$. The evaluation map $e:P\times\Delta^1\to B$ has endpoints $fr$ and $p$. Explicitly, on an $n$-simplex $(a,\gamma)$ of $P$, where $\gamma:\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\to B$ has initial endpoint $f(a)$, and $\theta:[n]\to[1]$, it is $\gamma\circ(1_{\Delta^n},\theta)$. This formula commutes with precomposition by $[m]\to[n]$, so defines the asserted evaluation map.

source.place: Proposition 3.6.3, path-space construction; agent-written mapping-path version and explicit evaluation formula

proof.text: Apply [lem-cbc-internal-hom-fibration-corner-map] with the degreewise inclusion $\partial\Delta^1=\{0\}\amalg\{1\}\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$ and the Kan fibration $B\to\Delta^0$. Its conclusion says that $(\operatorname{ev}_0,\operatorname{ev}_1):\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,B)\to B\times B$ is a Kan fibration. To fill a horn for $p$, let $u:\Lambda_k^m\to P$ and $v:\Delta^m\to B$ satisfy $pu=v|_{\Lambda_k^m}$. Since $A$ is Kan, extend $ru$ to $a:\Delta^m\to A$. The path coordinate of $u$ lies over $(fa,v)$ on the horn. Lift it through the displayed endpoint fibration to $\gamma:\Delta^m\to\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,B)$ over $(fa,v)$. Then $(a,\gamma)$ is the required filler in $P$. Thus $p$ is a Kan fibration, including both outer horns; this uses exactly the horn convention of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Theorem 3.3.1 and Proposition 3.6.3, endpoint path-space fibration; direct horn-lifting verification

proof.text:
Define $C:P\times\Delta^1\to P$ by
$$C((a,\gamma),t)=(a,[s\mapsto\gamma(\min(s,t))]).$$
This is a simplicial formula: pointwise minimum takes two monotone maps $[n]\to[1]$ to a monotone map and commutes with precomposition. More explicitly, for $(a,\gamma)\in P_n$ and $\theta:[n]\to[1]$, its new path is the composite of $\gamma$ with $(u,s)\mapsto(u,\min(s,\theta(u)))$ on $\Delta^n\times\Delta^1$. It still starts at $f(a)$, and its endpoint values at $t=0,1$ are $ir$ and $1_P$. The identities $ri=1_A$ and this homotopy meet [lem-cbc-simplicial-homotopy-equivalence-weak] for $u=i$, $v=r$ (use the constant homotopy on $A$). Hence $|i|$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. No interval-reversal map of simplicial sets is used.

source.place: Proposition 3.6.3 path construction and Lemma 3.4.6 monotone interval contractions; Kerodon 00UB forward implication supplies the cited homotopy-equivalence input

proof.text: The equality $f=pi$ realizes to $|f|=|p|\,|i|$. By the two-out-of-three assertion for realized weak homotopy equivalences in [lem-coef-topological-serre-model], the hypothesis on $|f|$ and step 3 imply that $|p|$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Step 2 and [lem-coef-kan-realization-serre] make $|p|$ a Serre fibration; that theorem does not require $P$ or $B$ to be Kan. Thus $|p|$ belongs to $F\cap W$ of the topological model structure. For any boundary lifting square $a:\partial\Delta^n\to P$, $b:\Delta^n\to B$ against $p$, [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits] identifies its realized left side with $S^{n-1}\hookrightarrow D^n$. These inclusions, including $\varnothing\hookrightarrow D^0$, are generating cofibrations in [lem-coef-topological-serre-model], hence have the left lifting property against $F\cap W$. The realized square therefore has a continuous filler $h$ with $|p|h=|b|$ and boundary value $|a|$.

source.place: Theorem 2.4.23, Corollary 3.6.2 and Theorem 3.6.4; the topological disk-lifting part of the comparison argument

proof.text: Apply [lem-cbc-kan-relative-realization-lift] to the Kan fibration $p$ of step 2 and each continuous filler of step 4. It produces a simplicial filler of every $\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ square against $p$, for all $n\geq0$. In dimension zero this says that $p_0$ is surjective, and in positive dimensions it is precisely the prescribed-boundary extension. These are exactly the clauses of [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration], so $p$ is a trivial Kan fibration.

source.place: Relative boundary-lifting comparison formulated in lem-cbc-kan-relative-realization-lift; identification with Stacks 08NL, definition-trivial-kan

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-lifts-monomorphisms] first for $\varnothing\hookrightarrow B$, with lower map $1_B$, to obtain a section $s:B\to P$, $ps=1_B$. Use it again for the degreewise injective endpoint map $P\amalg P\hookrightarrow P\times\Delta^1$. On the two ends prescribe $sp$ and $1_P$, and below prescribe $p\operatorname{pr}_P:P\times\Delta^1\to B$. This square commutes because $psp=p$. Its filler is a simplicial map $K:P\times\Delta^1\to P$ with $K_0=sp$, $K_1=1_P$ and $pK=p\operatorname{pr}_P$. The endpoint map is injective in every degree since the constant maps $[n]\to[1]$ with values $0$ and $1$ are distinct.

source.place: Tag 08NM, lemma-trivial-kan, lines 5550–5581; applied as in Tag 08NS, lemma-trivial-kan-homotopy, lines 5641–5664, with the desired endpoint order

proof.text:
Set $g=rs:B\to A$,
$$H=rK(i\times1_{\Delta^1}):A\times\Delta^1\to A,\qquad J=e(s\times1_{\Delta^1}):B\times\Delta^1\to B.$$
The endpoint equations follow by substitution:
$$H_0=rspi=rsf=gf,\quad H_1=ri=1_A,\quad J_0=frs=fg,\quad J_1=ps=1_B.$$
All maps used are simplicial by their displayed formulas and composition. No component or global basepoint was chosen. If one of $A,B$ is empty, the component bijection forces the other empty as well (any simplex has vertices); the unique empty maps satisfy the same equations. For disconnected complexes the argument applies unchanged, with the given weak-equivalence hypotheses on all components.
